description: God commands Moses to go to Pharaoh and demand the release of His people. This entire narrative block (the start of the second plague) is missing from OSMAIN.
The threat that if Pharaoh refuses, frogs will infest his borders. Missing from OSMAIN.
Detailed description of the frogs entering houses, bedrooms, beds, ovens, and kneading bowls. Missing from OSMAIN.
Statement that frogs will come upon Pharaoh, his people, and servants. Missing from OSMAIN.

OSMAIN v22 cuts off at 'dommernes avgjør'. Translation includes the full phrase 'og han skal betale etter dommernes avgjørelse' (and he shall pay as the judges determine). This is a truncation in OSMAIN.
OSMAIN v36 cuts off at 'sl'. Translation includes the full sentence regarding full restitution for a known goring ox. This is a truncation in OSMAIN.
Complete verse missing from OSMAIN. Contains laws about stealing an ox or sheep and the specific restitution penalties (5 oxen for one ox, 4 sheep for one sheep).

The entire verse (Deut 13:1) is missing from OSMAIN. It contains the command: 'You shall diligently keep all that I command you... do not add to it or take away from it.' This text precedes the false prophet scenario in standard Bibles but is absent here.
The entire verse: 'A man shall not take his father's wife, nor uncover his father's skirt.' This command is completely missing from the OSMAIN text provided.

The entire verse: 'A disse er ordene om den pakten Herren befalte Moses å slutte med israelittene i Moab, utenom den pakt han hadde sluttet med dem ved Horeb.' This content is completely missing from the OSMAIN text provided.

The verse 'וַיָּקָם וַיֵּלַךְ וִיהֹונָתָן בָּא הָעִיר׃' (Then Jonathan arose and went into the city) is present in the translation but has no corresponding text in the provided OSMAIN verses. The OSMAIN text starts directly with David's arrival at Nob.

The verse 'וַיֹּאמֶר שְׁלֹמֹה לִבְנֹות בַּיִת לְשֵׁם יְהוָה וּבַיִת לְמַלְכוּתֹו' (Solomon said to build a house for the name of the Lord and a house for his kingdom) is present in the translation but has no corresponding verse in the provided OSMAIN text, which ends at verse 17.

The WLC text completes the sentence regarding the bull and rams ('...and seven rams, and he shall be a priest for all who comes to fill his hand with a young bull of cattle and seven rams'). The provided OSMAIN text cuts off at 'b' (likely 'for to let himself be installed').

The WLC text completes the sentence regarding keeping God's commandments ('...because we keep our charge...'). The provided OSMAIN text cuts off at 'He' (likely 'For we hold fast to the He[avenly commands]').

Entire verse content: 'Abia slept with his fathers, and they buried him in the City of David. Asa his son reigned in his place. In his days the land was quiet for ten years.' This is a complete narrative unit missing from OSMAIN.
Sanballat's anger upon hearing the wall is being built (Nehemiah 4:1-2 equivalent).
Sanballat mocking the Jews and asking if they will finish in a day.
Tobiah's comment that a fox could break down their stone wall.
Prayer: 'Hear our God... turn their reproach back on them'.
Prayer: 'Do not cover their iniquity...'.
Narrative summary: The wall was joined together to half its height and the people had a mind to work.
Superscription/Title: 'To the choir director. With stringed instruments. A psalm of David.' This text is present as a header in OSMAIN v1 but separated into its own verse (v1) in WLC.

The mapping for v12 is actually 'exact' if we consider standard verse breaks. However, looking at WLC v13: 'כִּי-אַתָּה תְבָרֵךְ צַדִּיק יְהוָה כַצִנָּה רָצוֹן תַעטְרֶנוּ' (For Thou blessest the righteous; O Lord, with favor as a shield Thou coverest him). This text is completely absent from OSMAIN v1-v12. Therefore, WLC has an extra verse.
Contains unique content: 'For Thou blessest the righteous; O Lord, with favor as a shield Thou coverest him.' This text is missing from the OSMAIN source provided (which stops at v12).
OSMAIN verse 50 contains additional text ('He gives great victories to his king...') that corresponds to WLC verse 51. The mapping for WLC v50 is only the first part of OSMAIN v50.
This verse exists in the translation (WLC) but represents a split from OSMAIN verse 50. It does not contain content outside the scope of OSMAIN's text, it is just numbered differently.

Text: 'לְמַעַן יְזַמֶרְךָ כָבֹוד וְלֹא יִדּם יְהוָה אֱלֹהַי לְעֹולָם אֹודֶךָּ' (That my glory may sing your praise and not be silent. O Lord my God, I will give thanks to you forever). This verse is present in the WLC translation but missing from the provided OSMAIN text.

Superscription: 'To the choir director. Of the servant of David.' (לַמְנַצֵּחַ ׀ לְעֶבֶד־יְהוָה לְדָוִד׃). This text appears in WLC v1 but is missing from OSMAIN v1, which begins directly with the psalm content ('Sin speaks...').
Hurry to help me, Lord my salvation. This verse exists in the Hebrew text (wlc) but is not present in the provided OSMAIN list which ends at v22.

The entire content of verse 14 ('הָשַׁע מִמֶּנִּי וְאַבְלִיגָה בְּטֶרֶם אֵלֵךְ וְאֵינֶנִּי' - 'Turn from me that I may recover before I go and be no more') is missing in the OSMAIN text provided. In standard Hebrew numbering, this is often part of verse 13 or a distinct final plea not captured in the Norwegian master text's v13.
Text regarding making the name remembered forever and nations praising him is present in WLC v18 but absent from OSMAIN (which ends at verse 17).

Contains Hebrew superscription (Lamnatzeach...) and Psalm title which is not present in the OSMAIN text provided for verse 1. The OSMAIN v1 starts with 'Til korlederen' but lacks the full Hebrew script representation found here.
Superscription: 'To the choir director. A maskil of David.' This text is present in wlc but missing from the OSMAIN verse numbering provided (which starts with the narrative/historical note).
Superscription: 'To the choirmaster with stringed instruments; a maskil of David.' (לַמְנַצֵּחַ בִּנְגִינֹת מַשְׂכִּיל לְדָוִד)

Contains a plea for God to cast down men of blood and deceit into the pit (Psalm 55:23b-24 in standard numbering), which is not present in OSMAIN verse 23 or any other listed verse.

The translation ends with 'שֹׁפְטִים בָּאָרֶץ' (judges in the earth), whereas the provided OSMAIN text cuts off mid-sentence at 'som d'. The full Hebrew verse concludes the thought about God judging on earth, which is missing from the truncated OSMAIN source.

Superscription/Title: 'For the choir director. According to Jeduthun. A Psalm of David.' This text is present in WLC v1 but OSMAIN incorporates this title into its Verse 1 rather than having a separate verse for it.
Text: 'נָחִיתָ כַצֹּאן עַמֶּךָ בְּיַד־מֹשֶׁה וְאַהֲרֹן' (You led your people like a flock by the hand of Moses and Aaron). This verse is not present in OSMAIN.
WLC v19 contains a concluding doxology ('And let them know that thou...') which is absent in the OSMAIN text (which ends at verse 18).

The translation contains a full verse (v14) that corresponds to the second half of PSALM 60:12. The provided OSMAIN text for v13 ends with 'for human help is vain' and does not include the concluding line found in wlc v14 ('In God we shall do valiantly; He will tread down our enemies').
WLC v8 includes the concluding phrase 'also this is vanity and chasing after wind' (גַּם־זֶה הֶבֶל וְרָעוּת רוּחַ) which appears to be cut off or missing in the provided OSMAIN v8 text.
